summary: Aprepitant is a selective high-affinity substance P/neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor antagonist used with a 5-HT3 antagonist and a corticosteroid to prevent acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) and, at a lower dose, to prevent postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). It augments the antiemetic effect of ondansetron and dexamethasone. Because it is a substrate, weak-to-moderate inhibitor and inducer of CYP3A4 (and induces CYP2C9), it has important drug interactions, including reduced hormonal contraceptive efficacy and altered warfarin response.
indications: Prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting with highly emetogenic chemotherapy (including high-dose cisplatin), with other antiemetics, in patients >=12 years
Prevention of nausea and vomiting with moderately emetogenic chemotherapy, with other antiemetics, in patients >=12 years
Prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) in adults

dosage.d: 80 mg once daily in the morning
dosage.n: Give in the morning if no chemo on those days

dosage.d: 40 mg within 3 hours prior to induction of anesthesia
dosage.n: Acts as a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor at this dose

dosage.d: Reduce oral dexamethasone dose (e.g. ~50%) because aprepitant raises its levels

admin: Give the day-1 dose 1 hour before chemotherapy
May be administered with or without food; swallow capsules whole
Use as part of a combination regimen with a 5-HT3 antagonist and a corticosteroid
Reduce the dose of co-administered oral dexamethasone (CYP3A4 substrate)
Not intended for treatment of established nausea/vomiting or for chronic use
moa: Aprepitant is a selective, high-affinity antagonist at human substance P/neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptors, with little affinity for serotonin (5-HT3), dopamine or corticosteroid receptors. It crosses the blood-brain barrier and occupies central NK1 receptors, inhibiting both the acute and delayed phases of chemotherapy-induced emesis and augmenting the antiemetic activity of 5-HT3 antagonists and corticosteroids.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to aprepitant or any component (including anaphylaxis)
Concurrent use with pimozide (risk of QT prolongation from raised pimozide levels)
relative: Patients relying on hormonal contraception (reduced efficacy)
Patients on warfarin or other narrow-therapeutic-index CYP3A4/CYP2C9 substrates
monitor: Concomitant CYP3A4 substrates (e.g. some chemotherapy, midazolam, dexamethasone)

preg: There are insufficient data on aprepitant use in pregnant women to inform a drug-associated risk; animal studies at ~1.5 times human exposure showed no adverse developmental effects. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether aprepitant is excreted in human milk; it is present in the milk of lactating rats. Consider the benefits of breastfeeding and the mother's clinical need against any potential risk to the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed for renal impairment, including end-stage renal disease. Aprepitant is not removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh 5-9). There are no clinical or pharmacokinetic data in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh >9); use with caution.

major: Pimozide - contraindicated; increased pimozide levels can cause QT prolongation
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, clarithromycin) - markedly increase aprepitant levels
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin) - reduce aprepitant efficacy
CYP3A4-substrate chemotherapy and other sensitive CYP3A4 substrates - increased exposure
moderate: Oral corticosteroids (dexamethasone, methylprednisolone) - raised levels; reduce their dose
Warfarin - decreased INR (CYP2C9 induction); monitor INR for 2 weeks, particularly days 7-10
Hormonal contraceptives - reduced efficacy during and for 28 days after the last dose
Benzodiazepines metabolized by CYP3A4 (e.g. midazolam, alprazolam) - increased exposure
minor: Tolbutamide and other CYP2C9 substrates - reduced exposure
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal does not meaningfully affect bioavailability.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; chemotherapy-related lab changes (e.g. WBC, ALT) may be seen.

serious: Clinically significant drug interactions (e.g. with pimozide, chemotherapy)

monitoring: INR in patients on warfarin during the 2-week period (particularly days 7-10) after each aprepitant cycle
Adequacy of contraception (advise back-up non-hormonal method during and for 28 days after dosing)
Concomitant CYP3A4/CYP2C9 substrate levels and effects
Antiemetic efficacy and hydration in chemotherapy patients
counsel: Take the first dose one hour before chemotherapy and continue as prescribed
Hormonal birth control may not work during and for 28 days after treatment - use a back-up method
If you take warfarin, you will need extra INR checks
Tell your doctor about all your medicines, including over-the-counter and herbal products
Report rash, swelling of face/throat or difficulty breathing immediately
pk: Antiemetic protection during the day-1 dosing and the delayed phase
Covers acute and delayed (multi-day) emesis with the 3-day regimen
Store at controlled room temperature 20-25 C
pearls: Always use as part of a triple regimen (NK1 antagonist + 5-HT3 antagonist + corticosteroid) for highly emetogenic chemotherapy
Reduce co-administered oral dexamethasone dose by about half because aprepitant inhibits its CYP3A4 metabolism
Hormonal contraception can fail - advise a non-hormonal back-up during and for 28 days after the last dose
Monitor INR closely after each cycle in warfarin-treated patients (CYP2C9 induction lowers INR around days 7-10)
Pimozide is contraindicated; review all CYP3A4 substrates before prescribing
missed: Aprepitant is given as a short scheduled regimen around chemotherapy or surgery. If you miss a scheduled dose, contact your healthcare provider for instructions rather than doubling up; for the day-1 chemotherapy dose timing relative to treatment is important.
overdose: No specific antidote or treatment for overdose is established; drowsiness and headache occurred in a patient who took ~1,440 mg. Discontinue aprepitant and provide general supportive care and monitoring. Drug-induced emesis is unlikely to help because of aprepitant's antiemetic activity, and aprepitant is not removed by hemodialysis.
